item.title: Hwangnidan Street
item.script: There is a place in Gyeongju that is creating new history for the city. That place is Hwanglidan-gil Road, built by the hands of young entrepreneurs in Gyeongju. A few years ago, distinct and unique-looking shops started popping up one after another at a neighborhood in Hwangnam-dong, Gyeongju-si, set aside for redevelopment.  From cafes roasting aromatic coffee beans, characterful fusion restaurants, and retro pubs lighting up the streets at night, customers began pouring in Each shop had its own unique ambiance and ideas, which were perfect for satisfying younger generations in the Gyeongju area.  The narrow street soon became known as Hwanglidan-gil, and today, it continues to bustle with a never-ending stream of people. It was even listed on the “100 Must-Visit Tourist Spots of Korea” by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism recently. In other words, it has become an extremely popular destination among Korean people.   In less than five years, Hwanglidan-gil has transformed itself into a landmark representing the city of Gyeongju. It is so great to see young local entrepreneurs channel their love for the community and successfully create new hope. Don’t you agree? If you are interested, there are similar places brimming with passion such as Gonglidan-gil in Ulsan and Yeongildae in Pohang. Hwanglidan-gil blends a retro atmosphere that reminds people of the 1960s and 70s, and cultural elements that are distinctly from Shilla. So, come and interact with fun-loving young people at Hwanglidan-gil.  What makes this place even better is that it is full of people looking to live in harmony with one another. If you still think Gyeongju is like that old city you saw in your textbooks, you might be in for a surprise.

item.title: Entrance of Daereungwon Ancient Tombs
item.script: Daereungwon Ancient Tombs, the Tomb Complex, is a site where numerous ancient tombs from the Silla period are concentrated.  These ancient tombs are akin to museums in their own right. In ancient period, the dead were buried along with their personal belongings, grave goods, and sometimes even their servants. Consequently, ancient tombs serve as repositories of historical records and offer valuable insights into the culture of those times.  Daereungwon, in particular, boasts a remarkable collection of numerous old tombs, including the resting places of renowned kings and aristocrats. Here, 37 tombs are clustered together, and among them is the Hwangnamdaechong Tomb, the largest tomb in Gyeongju, a city famous for the discovery of a remarkable golden crown.  To begin your exploration, let's start with the tomb nearest to the entrance, which is the tomb of King Michu. As you enter, follow the path to your left, and then take the right fork. You will soon come across the protective walls that encircle the tomb.

item.title: Tomb of King Michu
item.script: The large tomb enclosed and protected by the walls is the tomb of King Michu. King Michu was a significant figure in Silla history, serving as the first King of Silla from the Kim family. During his reign, he exhibited a strong commitment to the development of the kingdom, defended it against foreign invasions, and promoted agricultural advancement. These efforts earned him profound respect from the people, a respect that continued even after his passing.  King Michu's tomb is also known by the nickname the bamboo tomb. This name has an interesting story behind it. During the reign of the 14th king of Silla, the kingdom faced an invasion from a neighboring nation. Silla was struggling in the battles, and the situation looked dire. Then, seemingly out of nowhere, an army of resolute soldiers appeared. Each of them wore helmets adorned with bamboo leaves and fought valiantly on behalf of Silla, eventually leading the kingdom to victory.  After the battle, these mysterious soldiers vanished without a trace, leaving only bamboo leaves behind. People came to believe that these bamboo leaf soldiers originated from the bamboo forest surrounding King Michu's tomb, and thus, they began to refer to it as the bamboo tomb. The legend persisted, with people thinking that King Michu was still watching over and assisting Silla, the kingdom he loved, even after his passing.

item.title: Entrance of Cheonmachong Tomb
item.script: If you take the left path from the Tomb of King Michu and continue until you pass a small lake, you'll come across the information office of Cheonmachong Tomb, located to the west of the lake.  The name Cheonmachong Tomb refers to the “tomb of a heavenly horse.” What makes it particularly noteworthy is that typically a tomb is named after its owner, the person who is buried under it. However, in the case of Cheonmachong Tomb, the identity of the owner has never been uncovered. As a result, it is named after the most famous treasure discovered within it, which is the painting of a heavenly horse.  Cheonmachong Tomb stands at a height of 12.7 meters and has a diameter of 47 meters. Researchers estimate that its construction would have required the efforts of approximately 200 workers laboring full-time every day for over six months. These grand and opulent royal tombs underscore the ruler's desire to display their authority and the strength of the regime.  Venturing inside the tomb provides a glimpse into Silla culture. The internal structure and interior of the tomb are adorned with replicas of artifacts that were excavated from it. The original artifacts are on display at the Gyeongju National Museum.
